what_happened: Job 20261030-060839-1njk (code job: "Refuse readings that drop a part the request names") failed in planning, before any code was written. After the last round (5 of 5) the critic still said the plan needed revising. The overall design was judged sound. Two major findings remained. (1) The request-side deferral rule ignores "later", "out of scope" and "for now", even in a sentence that names the part's marker. A faithful reading would be refused, and this also contradicts accepted criterion 4's "later" example. (2) Alternatives ("(a) ... or (b) ...") and optional parts are all treated as required, so a reading that picks one allowed option is refused with no honest repair. Six minor findings: terms.rs is not a deliverable; the Bullet marker is undefined; the sza7 fixture names the wrong checks.rs (crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs is the timeout file) and excuses it in the diff check; a deliverable path alone can cover a part, against the plan's own error text; and only an exact "Acceptance:" heading is recognised. No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Planning checks that named files and seams exist, but nothing makes the plan run a new refusal rule against the real request shapes it must accept: deferral wording, alternatives, optional parts and hand-written headings. The plan's deferral list, required-part assumption and heading match came from the reading's wording, not recorded past requests. Planning has fixed rounds, keeps no partial plan and has no repair step, so two major findings that survive round 5 lose all planning spend. This is the third attempt on this rule family.
other_causes: The plan names the wrong file (reading/checks.rs instead of crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs) and omits terms.rs from the deliverables, so nothing resolves each named path against the code before planning.
The plan contradicts an already accepted criterion (4's 'later' example) without saying so, and nothing cross-checks plan decisions against accepted criteria.
Several minor findings (undefined bullet marker, exact heading match) went unrepaired through five rounds.
open_hypotheses: The stored fields do not show whether earlier rounds fixed some findings while new ones appeared, so we cannot tell if the critic is converging.
Whether the request text itself allows alternatives or optional parts is not shown, so the second major finding may reflect an ambiguous request.
contradictions: The critic judged the overall design sound, with a shared filter, clear seams and demonstrations that fail without the step, which points against a design-level cause.
The earlier cases in this class were about invented fixtures. Here the worked stem examples came out as stated, so fixture invention is not the main gap.
prevention: Before planning ends, run any new reading-refusal rule automatically over a corpus of recorded past requests and accepted readings, and add the false refusals to the plan. The corpus should include deferral wording, alternatives, optional parts and varied Acceptance headings. Planning should hold the plan for a repair round when the only remaining findings are mechanical, instead of failing after round 5. Resolve each file path the plan names against the code before dispatch.
proposed_request: Refuse readings that drop a part the request names, as one change. Use crates/athena-core/src/reading/terms.rs and the other reading files as deliverables; the timeout checks.rs is crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs and is not touched. Acceptance: (1) A reading that omits a numbered or lettered part, or a bullet under an Acceptance list, that the request names is refused with an error saying to cover it with a deliverable and a criterion; a deliverable path alone does not cover a part. (2) A part is not counted as dropped when the request itself defers it, including with "later", "out of scope" or "for now", and a reading that follows that wording is accepted; this agrees with the accepted 'later' example in criterion 4. (3) Alternatives such as "(a) ... or (b) ..." and parts marked optional are satisfied by covering one option or by an explicit note; a reading that picks one allowed option is accepted. (4) Acceptance headings such as "Acceptance:", "Acceptance criteria:" and "## Acceptance" all open the bullet section; define the marker of a Bullet part. (5) The new step runs last in refusing_check, approved-work requests yield no parts after ## Source, and generated and copied text share one filter. (6) Replay the rule over the recorded past requests and accepted readings, including the standard Steward bullets, and report zero new false refusals. (7) fmt, clippy and test pass, and CHANGELOG.md gets an entry.
